78615.subject: Woodwork
78615.question_text:
Explain the differences between hardwood and softwood under the following headings:
(i) Botanical origin
(ii) Growth rate
(iii) Density and weight
(iv) Common uses in woodwork.
78615.explanation:
(i) Botanical origin: Hardwoods are derived from angiosperm trees (e.g., mahogany, wawa), which are flowering plants with enclosed seeds. Softwoods come from gymnosperm trees (e.g., pine, spruce), which are non-flowering and have exposed seeds.

(ii) Growth rate: Hardwoods generally grow slower than softwoods, resulting in denser and more durable timber. Softwoods grow faster, making them more readily available and often cheaper.

(iii) Density and weight: Hardwoods are typically denser and heavier due to their slower growth and tighter grain structure. Softwoods are lighter and less dense, which makes them easier to work with for certain applications.

(iv) Common uses in woodwork: Hardwoods are often used for high-quality furniture, flooring, and joinery due to their durability and aesthetic appeal. Softwoods are commonly used for construction framing, interior trim, and low-cost furniture.

78616.subject: Woodwork
78616.question_text: Name four types of timber commonly found in Ghana and state one specific use for each.
78616.explanation:
(i) Mahogany: Used for high-quality furniture, cabinetry, and veneers due to its durability and attractive grain.

(ii) Wawa: Commonly used for plywood, interior joinery, and light construction due to its lightweight and workability.

(iii) Odum: Used for heavy construction, bridges, and outdoor furniture because of its resistance to decay and termites.

(iv) Ofram: Often used for flooring, paneling, and boat building due to its strength and resistance to moisture.

78617.subject: Woodwork
78617.question_text: Describe two methods of seasoning timber and explain two defects that may occur if timber is improperly seasoned.
78617.explanation:
Methods of seasoning:
(i) Air Seasoning: Timber is stacked in a well-ventilated area, protected from direct sunlight and rain, allowing moisture to evaporate naturally over several months.
(ii) Kiln Seasoning: Timber is placed in a kiln where temperature, humidity, and airflow are controlled to reduce moisture content rapidly and uniformly.

Defects from improper seasoning:
(i) Warping: Uneven drying causes timber to bend or twist out of shape.
(ii) Checking: Rapid drying leads to cracks or splits along the grain of the timber.

78618.subject: Woodwork
78618.question_text: Which of the following timber conversion methods is most suitable for producing wide, flat boards with minimal waste?
78618.explanation: The quarter sawing method is designed to produce wide, flat boards with minimal waste by cutting the log radially. This method also enhances the stability and appearance of the timber by reducing warping and highlighting the grain.

78619.subject: Woodwork
78619.question_text: Explain two methods of preserving timber and state one advantage of each method.
78619.explanation:
(i) Pressure Treatment: Timber is placed in a pressure vessel where preservative chemicals are forced deep into the wood fibers. Advantage: Provides long-lasting protection against decay, insects, and fungi.

(ii) Brush or Spray Application: Preservative chemicals are applied to the surface of the timber using a brush or spray. Advantage: Simple, cost-effective, and suitable for small-scale projects or touch-ups.

78620.subject: Woodwork
78620.question_text: Which of the following manufactured boards is most suitable for making curved furniture components?
78620.explanation: Plywood is the most suitable manufactured board for making curved furniture components because it is flexible, strong, and can be bent into various shapes without breaking.

78621.subject: Woodwork
78621.question_text: Describe the correct procedure for maintaining a hand plane to ensure its efficiency and longevity.
78621.explanation:
(i) Cleaning: Remove dust and shavings from the plane after each use using a brush or cloth.
(ii) Sharpening the Blade: Regularly sharpen the plane iron using a whetstone or oilstone to maintain a keen edge.
(iii) Adjusting the Blade: Ensure the blade is properly aligned and set to the correct depth for smooth cutting.
(iv) Lubrication: Apply a light coat of oil to metal parts to prevent rust and ensure smooth operation.
(v) Storage: Store the plane in a dry place, preferably in a toolbox or on a rack, to protect it from damage and moisture.

78622.subject: Woodwork
78622.question_text: Sketch and describe two types of basic wood joints, stating one specific use for each.
78622.explanation:
(i) Butt Joint: The simplest joint where two pieces of wood are joined end-to-end or edge-to-edge. Use: Commonly used in framing and basic construction where strength is not critical.

(ii) Lap Joint: Two pieces of wood overlap each other, providing more surface area for gluing and increased strength. Use: Often used in cabinet making and furniture construction for joining shelves or dividers.

78623.subject: Woodwork
78623.question_text: Which of the following personal protective equipment (PPE) is most essential when operating a circular saw?
78623.explanation: Safety goggles are the most essential PPE when operating a circular saw to protect the eyes from flying debris and wood particles.

78624.subject: Woodwork
78624.question_text:
Explain the following principles of furniture design:
(i) Proportion
(ii) Balance
(iii) Harmony
(iv) Functionality.
78624.explanation:
(i) Proportion: Refers to the relationship between the sizes of different parts of a piece of furniture. Good proportion ensures that no single part dominates the design, creating a visually pleasing and cohesive piece.

(ii) Balance: The distribution of visual weight in a design. Balance can be symmetrical (mirror image) or asymmetrical (unequal but balanced elements), ensuring stability and aesthetic appeal.

(iii) Harmony: The consistent use of design elements such as color, texture, and shape to create a unified and cohesive look. Harmony ensures that all parts of the furniture piece work together seamlessly.

(iv) Functionality: The practical use and ergonomics of the furniture. A well-designed piece must serve its intended purpose effectively while being comfortable and user-friendly.
